sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text:
Compared with G. suturis the alate has a narrower and shorter head and pronotum, a more shallowly concave posterior margin of the pronotum with less rounded sides, and ocelli that do not touch the eyes; compared with G. pellucidus the head and wings are narrower and shorter, the eyes smaller, and the ocelli do not touch the eyes. The soldier differs from those of the other known Neotropical species in the long, narrow and thin head that is broad anteriorly.

The type locality is Córdoba, Veracruz, Mexico (18°55′ N, 96°55′ W); the alates (morphotype and paramorphotypes), soldiers (holotype and paratypes) and nymphs were collected by C. H. Seevers on 21 July 1936 (month 7), and soldier paratypes and nymphs were collected on 22 July of the same year (month 7). The species is named after Dr C. H. Seevers, professor of zoology at Roosevelt University, Chicago.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head, pronotum and abdomen brownish yellow; a rounded pale spot on each side of the frons; pronotum paler than the head, with a dark T-shaped mark in the middle; antennae and legs pale yellow; wings smoky brown. Head with a few sparse erect setae; margins of the pronotum with numerous setae, the disc with a few. Head width almost equal to the head length (to the base of the mandibles). Y-suture faintly visible. Eyes shaped as figured. Ocelli pear-shaped, very close to the eyes (0.01 mm apart). Antennae 13-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 longer than segment 4. Pronotum narrower than the head, anterior margin angular, sides slightly rounded, posterolateral margins broadly rounded or straight and meeting the straight posterior margin at an angle. The media of the hindwing arises from the radial sector beyond the wing scale, about 0.90 mm from the wing suture.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head brown, the frontal region reddish brown; mandibles dark reddish brown; labrum pale yellow; pronotum, antennae and legs pale brown. Head with a few sparse setae; margins and disc of the pronotum with both long and short setae; labrum with 10—11 erect setae. Head long, narrow posteriorly, widest anteriorly; middle of the frons slightly concave, forming a slope of about 45° in lateral view. Y-suture visible as a pale line. Eyes small and blurred. Labrum small, sides straight, anterior margin rounded. Mandibles short and stout, outer margin almost straight; left mandible with 3 very small marginal teeth resembling a serrulation, the first largest; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, the tip of the first marginal tooth lying 0.35 mm from the tip of the apical tooth. Postmentum long, the sides converging strongly backwards from the widest point and running parallel for a short stretch before flaring again. Antennae 11—13-segmented, segment 3 shortest, segment 4 slightly longer than segment 3 and shorter than segment 2. Pronotum narrower than the head, anterior margin angular, anterolateral corners narrow, posterolateral margins broadly rounded, posterior margin with a broad median concavity.

Soldier measurements (holotype; paratypes from the type nest n=2; the other series of paratypes n=5): head length (to the base of the mandibles) 2.02 mm / 1.88—2.02 mm / 2.18—2.33 mm; head width 1.09 mm / 1.03—1.09 mm / 1.15—1.22 mm; head height 0.98 mm / 0.98 mm / 1.07—1.13 mm; length of the left mandible 0.90 mm / 0.90 mm / 0.97 mm; postmentum maximum width 0.39 mm / 0.38—0.39 mm / 0.38—0.45 mm; postmentum minimum width 0.19 mm / 0.19 mm / 0.15—0.17 mm; postmentum length 1.46 mm / 1.35—1.46 mm / 1.58—1.73 mm; pronotum median length 0.47 mm / 0.45—0.47 mm / 0.49—0.56 mm; pronotum maximum length 0.60 mm / 0.56—0.60 mm / 0.60—0.70 mm; pronotum width 0.92 mm / 0.83—0.92 mm / 0.98—1.05 mm; length of the hind tibia 0.83 mm / 0.83 mm / 0.87—0.90 mm.
